# Ten-language catalog snapshot v2 fixtures

Generated by `node tooling/scripts/tasks/server.mjs desktop-fixtures` in temporary PostgreSQL/Redis instances using the production snapshot service and real HTTP handlers. Time is fixed at 2026-10-01; no development database content is read, translated or backfilled.

- `catalog.json.gz`: base snapshot with 40 Casks, 20 categories and cursor 60; includes sourceLocale but no localized text.
- `text-{locale}.json.gz`: actual text packs for the ten desktop languages. Japanese includes the temporary seed's “日本語エディター” and category “開発ツール”. Objects without content in the other eight languages remain absent; English must not be copied to fill them.
- `latest.json`: unwrapped CDN metadata; `snapshot.json`: HTTP response with code/msg/data. Both list only the original six packs, the contract of clients up to 0.1.16 (0.1.13 and older reject other language keys). `snapshot-all.json` is the `locales=all` response the ten-language client reads, with every pack. Metadata bytes/SHA-256 match the committed gzip files.
- `changes-page.json`, `changes-final.json`, `changes-empty.json`: real deltas and paired complete category data, using cursors 61–64. They are the legacy responses without `locales=all`, so category names cover the original six languages.
- `changes-expired.json`: HTTP 410/code 1201 response body; `client-config.json`: client configuration.

Rust tests read these files locally and also use random loopback ports to verify that switching to Japanese downloads only the Japanese pack, request headers use the new language, bad hashes and mid-transaction failures preserve the old database, Japanese offline search works, deltas remove missing translations, and old SQLite migrations preserve tasks and cached text. The parent directory's v1 files remain for migration compatibility regression tests; new publication and HTTP sync use v2.
